discovery.description: DeepSeek Harness desktop CLI (D:\Program Next\dsh\DeepSeek Harness.exe) --profile acp

capabilities.notes: DeepSeek Harness ACP over ndJSON stdio (`dsh --profile acp`). Verified against the desktop-bundled CLI 0.2.1-rc.5 (agent 0.0.1): initialize advertises ACP v1 plus session close/list/resume, session/new and session/resume work, model and reasoning_effort are selectable config options, session/prompt blocks until the turn and descendants settle, session/cancel returns stopReason=cancelled, and stdin EOF exits the process cleanly. session/resume restores the persisted conversation in a new process and requires the identical absolute cwd; there is no session/load, fork, delete or transcript replay. The shipped acp profile reads DSH_PERMISSION_MODE at boot and defaults to workspace-write with approval ask: file writes inside the workspace or platform temp are allowed without a prompt, while an outside write is denied and can trigger session/request_permission for a one-time danger-full-access escalation (verified). HARNESS_SUPERVISOR_DSH_PERMISSION_MODE selects read-only, workspace-write or danger-full-access; danger-full-access removes the file sandbox and sets approval to never. DSH's permission request carries only a tool call id, not the tool name or input; the adapter answers with the offered allow-once/reject-once option. ACP has no active-turn steer, so steer and follow-up are unsupported; a second prompt is rejected while one is active. No plan, commands, terminal, client filesystem, elicitation, MCP stdio or images. usage_update is context occupancy, not billed token usage. DSH's ACP codec maps native aborted/blocked/error turn endings to end_turn, so HS cannot always distinguish those from a normal completion. cwd is not a filesystem sandbox.

limits.permissions: The acp profile reads DSH_PERMISSION_MODE at boot and defaults to workspace-write with approval ask. A write inside the workspace or platform temp needs no approval; an outside write is denied and triggers session/request_permission for a one-time danger-full-access escalation. HARNESS_SUPERVISOR_DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access removes the file sandbox and approval, and an outside write then succeeds without a request. The desktop permission picker only configures desktop sessions and does not apply to the acp profile.
limits.steering: ACP has no active-turn steer; capabilities report steer=false and followUp=false.
limits.usage: usage_update is context occupancy, not billed token usage; HS records it as context_usage progress, not run.usage.
